title: Canary A/B divergence due to KV-cache + quantization mismatch — incident follow-up, runbook & simulation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a staged A/B canary (model-v2 vs model-v2-quantized) we observed a progressive semantic-quality degradation for 2% of user traffic that only manifested under the production request prefix distribution. Auto-rollback triggered on increased utility-regression alerts, but the fallback path partially failed because the quantized variant used a different KV cache layout which produced cache misses and increased latency; this in turn amplified model temperature differences and caused flapping between rollbacks and re-rollouts. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups: telemetry contract gaps, runbook updates, synthetic failure-injection plan, and automation guardrails to prevent recurrence.
postmortem_summary: Root cause was a compatibility gap between model-variant kernel/quantization settings and the live KV cache layout. Canary traffic exercised long-tail prompt prefixes that exposed higher KL divergence in outputs for the quantized variant. Telemetry only tracked token-level errors and latency but not semantic drift. Auto-rollback logic used a single aggregate alert which oscillated under noisy signals. Impact: ~24 hours of intermittent inference-quality regressions for small subset of customers (estimated <1% requests), plus two emergency rollbacks that increased engineer on-call load. No data exfiltration or stability SLO breach beyond latency spikes for affected buckets.

runbook_updates: Add 'compatibility-check' step to pre-canary checklist: validates kernel + quantization + KV cache layout on canary infra nodes.
Introduce explicit 'freeze-canary' command that prevents re-rollouts until a PM/Eng review sign-off is recorded in the rollout metadata.
Define escalation ladder: Level 1 (canary metric owners), Level 2 (runtime leads), Level 3 (on-call SRE + PM), with 30m SLA for acknowledgement.
Include a guided reproducibility run in the runbook that uses the synthetic traffic harness and deterministically seeded RNG to replicate the regression locally.
Document fallback behaviors: if fallback model uses incompatible KV layout, route to safe generic-encoder model and notify SRE.
safety_checks_added: Pre-rollout 'mini-eval' that computes per-route embedding-distance drift vs baseline (threshold: mean+3σ).
KV layout checksum verification step: nodes must report identical cache-format hash before accepting variant.
Model-variant compatibility matrix enforced by CI: kernel options and quantization flags must match supported runtime profiles.
Canary stability gate: require stable semantic-quality signal for 12 hours at 1% traffic before scaling to >5%.
Auto-rollback hysteresis: use 3-window majority for trigger to avoid flapping under noisy single-window spikes.
telemetry_changes: New metric 'sem_quality_kl' computed per-route using fixed prompt set and reference outputs; emitted to main metrics pipeline every 5m.
Per-request metadata tagging with 'kv_layout_hash' and 'kernel_profile' for sample-based tracing.
Add alert 'canary_semantic_regression' that combines embedding-distance and KL signals with anomaly score to reduce false positives.
Dashboard panels: per-canary split view showing semantic metrics, token-latency P95, cache-miss rate, and rollback signals side-by-side.
Retention change: keep 30d of canary-level semantic metrics with 1h rollup for trend analysis.
simulation_plan: Build 'synthetic-prefix-generator' to replay production-like prefix distributions (derived from sampled anonymized prefix histogram) with deterministic seeds.
Failure-injection scenarios: (A) force KV-cache-miss on 10% of requests; (B) swap kernel_profile to 'mixed-quant' to simulate quantization edge-cases; (C) inject 50ms extra latency on fallback path.
Run nightly simulation matrix across model variants and runtimes with summary report uploaded to Confluence and linked in rollout metadata.
Add CI job 'canary-sim' that runs a fast subset of scenarios for every model-variant PR and blocks merge on critical regressions.
